issues.legal_issue: An adjudication by a competent court between the parties on the validity of the same instruments binds them in later proceedings even if erroneous, and prevents a later claim based on those instruments from succeeding.
material_facts: In earlier litigation between the parties, the validity of the gift deeds was challenged and a competent court held the deeds invalid; that determination was affirmed on appeal.
In the later partition suit, a party relied on the deeds and a family settlement to claim title, and the appellate court rejected that claim in light of the earlier adjudication.
The appeal challenged the later appellate decision.
issues.conclusion: The earlier adjudication was binding between the parties, so the deeds could not support a later claim of title. The appellate court was justified in rejecting the claim, and the appeal was dismissed. The Court did not need to decide the separate argument that family arrangements should be enforced through estoppel.
issues.legal_principle: A judgment between parties binds them when a court of competent jurisdiction has decided the lis, even if the judgment is erroneous. Although Kale v. Deputy Director of Consolidation, (1976) 3 SCC 119, was cited for the principle that courts generally favour honest family arrangements and may use estoppel to preserve them, that principle did not require consideration here because the validity of the gift deeds had already been adjudicated between the parties.

predicates.appeal_in_later_partition_proceeding: A party appealed from a decision in a later proceeding seeking partition or a related claim of title.
predicates.prior_competent_court_decided_validity_o: A court with jurisdiction decided the validity of the instruments on which a later claim relies.
predicates.prior_litigation_involved_same_parties: The earlier litigation over those instruments involved the parties bound by the later proceeding.
predicates.prior_inter_party_judgment_binds_parties: The earlier adjudication binds the parties in the later proceeding, even if it was erroneous.

issues.definition: When a party appeals in a later partition proceeding and a competent court had already decided the validity of the same instruments in litigation involving the same parties, the earlier adjudication binds those parties.
